earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog: retired entry, 'based on a misunderstanding to begin with'; no references listed.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2018. Change Request Number 2018-016: adopted retire [lba] (effective 2019-01-25). SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing. Retires [lba] as non-existent: 'Nowhere is Lui represented as a language but is used as an ethnonym or cover term for a group of languages' (Andro, Sengmai, Chairel of Manipur, extinct, related to Sak/Chak [ckh]); cites Damant 1880, Voegelin & Voegelin 1977, Hammarstrom (Glottolog) calling Lui spurious.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2011. Change Request Number 2011-092: adopted update [lba] (2012-02-03). SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing. States (citing Loeffler 1964 p.21 and the Linguistic Survey of India) that the 'Lui' of Manipur spoke Andro, Sengmai and Chairel, that these died out before the LSI, and that 'the only existing wordlist is MacCulloch 1859' (Luce 1985's data derive from it).

sources.citation: Glottolog languoid pages for Sengmai (seng1275), Andro (andr1246), Chairel (chai1254) — search results.
sources.note: Nothing; each is an extinct variety 'documented by a wordlist in McCulloch, W. 1859' only.

sources.citation: Hammarstrom, Forkel, Haspelmath & Bank. Glottolog: languoid page 'Lui' luia1234 (Bookkeeping).
sources.note: Nothing. Page: 'This entry has been retired and is featured here only for bookkeeping purposes.. it was based on a misunderstanding to begin with'; retirement reason 'non-existent'; zero descriptive references.

sources.citation: Loeffler, Lorenz G. 1964. Chakma und Sak: ethnolinguistische Beitraege zur Geschichte eines Kulturvolkes. Internationales Archiv fuer Ethnographie 50(1): 72-115.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Cited in CR 2011-092 (p.21) as the discussion establishing that the Lui varieties were extinct and known only from McCulloch 1859; would confirm there is no phonological description. Not a stress source.

sources.citation: McCulloch, W. 1859. Account of the Valley of Munnipore and of the Hill Tribes; with a comparative vocabulary of the Munnipore and other languages. (Selections from the Records of the Government of India, Foreign Department, 27.) Calcutta.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The sole primary attestation of Andro/Sengmai/Chairel ('Lui') per both ISO change requests; a comparative vocabulary only, so it almost certainly says nothing about stress, but it is the only place any first-hand data live. Low value for a stress catalog.
